questions.q: Why is training strictly in proportion to each data source's raw token count usually suboptimal?
options: It is actually always optimal and labs never deviate from it
Web text vastly dwarfs higher-value sources like books or Wikipedia in raw token count, even though per-token value for reasoning and knowledge is not equal across domains
Raw proportions are illegal to use under data licensing law
Proportional sampling makes the tokenizer fail
questions.explain: Because web crawl data is far larger by volume than curated sources, training purely in proportion would overweight highly variable web text relative to denser, higher-value sources -- so labs deliberately depart from raw proportions.

questions.q: What does 'upsampling' a data domain mean in the context of mixture weighting?
options: Increasing a domain's effective sampling frequency beyond its natural proportion in the raw collected data
Deleting that domain from the training set entirely
Converting that domain's text into a different language
Reducing the vocabulary size used for that domain
questions.explain: Upsampling means repeating or oversampling a smaller, higher-value domain relative to how often it would naturally appear given its raw size, so the model sees it more often than its true proportion.

questions.q: What does Hugging Face's `interleave_datasets` function do when given a `probabilities` argument?
options: It deduplicates the combined dataset
It draws from multiple source datasets according to the specified sampling probabilities, regardless of each dataset's actual size
It trains a tokenizer directly
It automatically ranks datasets by quality score
questions.explain: interleave_datasets samples from the given list of datasets according to the probabilities provided, letting a smaller but valuable dataset be deliberately overrepresented relative to its true size.

questions.q: What problem does DoReMi (Domain Reweighting with Minimax Optimization) address?
options: It removes the need for a tokenizer entirely
Hand-picking mixture weights through trial and error is expensive since each candidate weighting requires its own costly evaluation run
It eliminates the need for deduplication
It replaces GQA with standard multi-head attention
questions.explain: DoReMi trains a small proxy model with a minimax objective to learn domain weights automatically, avoiding the need to run expensive full-scale training for every candidate hand-picked mixture.

questions.q: Why is mixture weighting described as one of the highest-leverage decisions in the data pipeline?
options: It has no real effect on the trained model
It determines how often the model sees each domain, which directly shapes the balance of knowledge and skills the resulting model ends up with
It only affects the speed of the tokenizer, not model quality
It is the only stage of the pipeline that uses any code at all
questions.explain: While earlier stages determine what data is available and how it's represented, mixture weighting determines how often the model actually sees each domain during training, directly shaping its resulting knowledge and skill balance.
